videos.script: A password proves very little. It gets guessed, reused, and typed into a fake page. {{password}} So Azure now asks for a second factor from everybody who manages it. In the portal since 2024, and in the command line since October 2025. {{mandatory}} A small tenant can switch on security defaults. One fixed set of rules, the same for everyone. {{defaults}} A larger one writes its own rules. That is conditional access. {{ca}} A rule says: if these people reach these applications, under these conditions, then ask for this. Or block them. {{rule}} Every rule that applies is enforced at once. There is no first match. {{all}} So a new rule starts in report-only. It writes down what it would have done, and does nothing. {{report}} And before any rule is enforced, two emergency accounts exist, outside every rule, watched every time they sign in. {{breakglass}} The way out has to be built before the door is locked. {{end}}
